_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 5 Mathematics unit lecture film, Past the Whole Numbers. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Grade 5 is a page a learner scans, not a deck: this film sits above the lesson's five static steps and does not replace them. The chapters follow the lesson's own WORK parts, in order (Place value with decimals; Negative numbers and rounding; Fractions, percentages and ratio), each split into one chapter per idea: decimals (step 23), moving the digits (step 24), negative numbers (step 22), rounding (step 21), fractions and percentages (steps 25-26), ratio and proportion (step 27). Every number said is the lesson's own: 0.65 vs 0.7, 3.5 x 10 = 35, 5 degrees C and negative 3 degrees C, 149 rounding straight to 100 (never via 150), 3.7 rounds to 4 but 4.5 rounds to 5, 65% = 65/100 = 0.65, and the 3:2 counter mix. The lesson's own two flagged wrong claims (3.7 and 4.5 both rounding to 4; Pia's 15.73 = 10 + 5.7 + 0.3) are never asserted as true; the film corrects the first directly.
title: Past the Whole Numbers
subtitle: Grade 5 Mathematics
objectives: Understand and explain the value of each digit in decimals (tenths and hundredths).
Use knowledge of place value to multiply and divide whole numbers by 10, 100 and 1000.
Use knowledge of place value to multiply and divide decimals by 10 and 100.
Understand the relative size of quantities to compare and order positive and negative numbers, using the symbols =, > and <.
Round numbers with one decimal place to the nearest whole number.
Recognise that proper fractions, decimals (one decimal place) and percentages can have equivalent values.
Understand that: a proportion compares part to whole a ratio compares part to part of two or more quantities.

beats.say: Numbers do not stop at the ones column. They carry on, in both directions.
Today: past the decimal point, and below zero into negatives.
Place value carries on past the point too.
The first column after the point is tenths. The next is hundredths.
Each column is worth ten times less than the one before it.
0.65 has more digits written down than 0.7, but it is the smaller number.
The comparison is decided in the tenths column: seven tenths beats six tenths.
Multiplying by ten is taught as add a zero. That only works for whole numbers.
3.5 times ten is 35 - not 3.50.
What really happens: every digit moves one column to the left.

at.moves: every digit moves one column to the left

beats.say: The point stays exactly where it always was.

at.stays: The point stays exactly where it always was

beats.say: Dividing goes backwards: one column for ten, two for a hundred, three for a thousand.
Counting down from 5 carries on past zero: negative 1, negative 2, negative 3.
Morning was 5 degrees. Night was negative 3 degrees.
That is 8 degrees apart: 5 steps down to zero, then 3 more.
The minus sign shows which side of zero, not how big the number is.

at.big: not how big the number is

beats.say: So negative 7 is lower than negative 3, though 7 is bigger than 3.
Rounding reads just one digit: the one right after the place.

at.after: the one right after the place

beats.say: 149 to the nearest ten is 150.
Round straight from 149, not twice - to the nearest hundred it is 100, not 200.
Exactly halfway always rounds up. Everyone agrees, so everyone gets the same answer.
The same rule works on decimals: 3.7 rounds to 4, but 4.5 rounds to 5, not 4.
A fraction cuts a whole into equal parts. The bottom number counts the cuts.

at.cuts: cuts a whole into equal parts
at.bottom: The bottom number counts the cuts

beats.say: 1/4 has the bigger bottom number, but it is the smaller amount.
0.65 is a fraction too: 65 out of 100, or 13 out of 20.
Per cent means for each hundred, so 65% is 65 out of 100 as well.

at.percent: Per cent means for each hundred

beats.say: 65%, 65/100 and 0.65 are one number, three different costumes.
This mix has 3 orange counters and 2 teal ones.
A ratio compares part to part: 3 to 2, written 3:2.

at.ratio: A ratio compares part to part

beats.say: 3:2 does not mean the fraction 3/2 - both numbers are just parts.
Add the parts for the whole: 3 plus 2 is 5 counters in all.

at.addParts: Add the parts for the whole

beats.say: 3 out of 5 is a proportion, part to whole: 60%.
Place value carries on past the point, and past zero into negatives.
Times ten moves every digit one column left. The point never moves.

at.moves: moves every digit one column left

beats.say: Round on the one digit after the place, straight from the start, every time.

at.oneDigit: the one digit after the place

beats.say: A fraction, a decimal and a percentage can be one number. A ratio is part to part.
